hero.heading: Ecommerce analytics that survives cookie consent
hero.subheading: GA4 loses a large share of EU traffic to consent banners, and event-priced tools scale into the thousands. OpenPanel tracks every cart, checkout and purchase without cookies, with revenue attached, from $2.50 a month or free to self-host.

problem.title: Why ecommerce analytics is broken in 2026
problem.intro: Every analytics tool has a different failure mode for online stores. Here's what actually breaks.

items.title: Cookie consent destroys GA4 data
items.description: Under GDPR you need explicit consent for analytics cookies, and a large share of EU shoppers click reject. GA4 fills the gap with modeled data, so you optimise ad spend on estimates.

items.title: Event-priced analytics scale into the thousands
items.description: Mixpanel and Heap charge per event. A busy store firing 50 events a session reaches 1M events at 20K sessions. That is hundreds a month before any decision has been made with the data.

items.title: Shopify and WooCommerce native reports are shallow
items.description: Pageviews and orders are there, but you cannot build a funnel from product page to cart to checkout, segment by acquisition channel, or compare retention by product. Native reports show what happened, not why.

items.title: Cart-abandonment retargeting depends on attribution that breaks
items.description: When a third of shoppers reject cookies and the rest are cleared by browser tracking prevention, last-click attribution stops matching reality.

features.title: Everything an online store needs
features.intro: These features cover the full ecommerce funnel without the privacy or pricing trade-offs.

items.title: Cookieless tracking by default
items.description: No cookies, no consent banner, no modeled data. Every visitor counts, every event lands in the database, and your conversion data isn't filtered by opt-out rates.

items.title: Revenue tracking
items.description: Send the amount with the purchase event and it follows the session and the customer. Revenue shows on the overview, next to sources, campaigns and entry pages, and on every profile. One currency, shown as USD.

items.title: Funnels broken down by product
items.description: Build product page to add to cart to checkout to purchase, then break the funnel down by a product, category or campaign property. See where each product loses customers.

items.title: Works with Shopify, WooCommerce, Stripe and custom stacks
items.description: Drop the script tag into a Shopify or WordPress theme, or use an SDK in a Next.js or Remix store. Purchases are revenue events you send from the thank-you page or from your payment webhook. No native integrations, no app to install.

items.title: EU-only data residency
items.description: Cloud data is stored on Hetzner in Germany, with backups inside the EU. One GDPR data processing agreement covers it; no transfer impact assessments or Standard Contractual Clauses to maintain.

items.title: Customer profiles and lifetime revenue
items.description: Every customer with the ad they came from, the products they viewed, their purchases and their lifetime revenue. Repeat purchases show up in retention.

items.title: Realtime dashboard
items.description: Run a flash sale or send an email and watch traffic and revenue land live. No processing delay.

items.title: Self-host for unlimited events
items.description: Run OpenPanel on your own infrastructure with Docker Compose for a flat hosting cost. The install is one script. Self-hosted releases follow Cloud by a month or two.

faqs.title: Frequently asked questions
faqs.intro: Common questions from ecommerce teams evaluating OpenPanel.

items.question: Can OpenPanel replace GA4 for an online store?
items.answer: Yes. OpenPanel covers the core ecommerce reporting GA4 does (pageviews, traffic sources, UTM attribution, conversion events, revenue, funnels) and adds cohorts, retention, customer profiles and session replay. The biggest difference is that OpenPanel is cookieless, so the consent banner can go and the data is complete.

items.question: How do I install OpenPanel on Shopify?
items.answer: Add the OpenPanel script tag in Shopify Admin, Online Store, Themes, Edit code, theme.liquid, before </head>. Pageviews track automatically. For purchases, call op.revenue(amount, { orderId, products }) on the order confirmation page after enabling client-side revenue in project settings. See the [Shopify analytics page](/for/shopify).

items.question: How do I install OpenPanel on WooCommerce?
items.answer: Install the OpenPanel WordPress plugin and paste your client id, or add the script tag to your theme header. For orders, hook into WooCommerce's woocommerce_thankyou action and send a revenue event with the order total. Add-to-cart and product views are custom events you fire from the same hooks.

items.question: Does OpenPanel work with Stripe Checkout or Payment Links?
items.answer: Yes. Fire a checkout_started event from the product page when a customer clicks buy, then send op.revenue(amount, { orderId }) from your Stripe webhook handler when checkout.session.completed arrives, using the client secret. This works for Stripe Checkout, Payment Links, Subscriptions and Elements.

items.question: Will I need a cookie consent banner with OpenPanel on my store?
items.answer: Not for analytics. OpenPanel sets no cookies and stores no raw IP, so a consent banner is not needed for analytics under GDPR or CCPA. You may still need one for marketing pixels (Meta, Google Ads) if you use them.

items.question: Will OpenPanel slow down my checkout?
items.answer: The web tracker is about 3 KB gzipped and loads async; GA4 is many times larger. The impact at checkout is well below anything that moves Core Web Vitals or conversion.

items.question: How does OpenPanel pricing compare to Mixpanel for a busy store?
items.answer: A store with 20K sessions a month and 50 events a session fires 1M events. Mixpanel charges a few hundred a month at that volume. OpenPanel Cloud is $90 a month for 1M events, or free self-hosted. In a Black Friday spike you move up a flat tier rather than paying overages.

items.question: Can I track multi-store setups (Shopify Plus with multiple stores)?
items.answer: Yes. Projects are unlimited, so track each store as its own project, or put them in one project and break reports down by a store_id property. Both work.
